messages:
Zoe Lin: Heads-up — nightly-h100 CI is red, 3/3 runs failing in warmup with 'invalid device function' during kernel launch. Job: quant-infer-e2e. Logs attached.
ci-bot: build #3456 failed on h100-nightly (quant-infer-e2e). logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/3456
Ryan: @Zoe can you paste the failing log snippet? first guess: driver/container mismatch or bad kernel compile.
Zoe Lin: snippet below:
```
E cuda: invalid device function (code=8) at /workspace/runtime/kernel_launch.cu:42
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "./run.py", line 128, in <module>
    warmup_kernel()
RuntimeError: cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction: invalid device function
```
Maria: I also noticed Xid 139 in dmesg on that node earlier today :thinking: Node id h100-114.
Arjun: if it's libcuda/driver mismatch, symptoms look like that. Which libcuda version inside container? Can you run `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so` or `strings /usr/local/cuda/version.txt`?
Sam: oncall — I'll ssh to h100-114 and run a quick check.
Zoe Lin: minimal repro command:
```
docker run --gpus=all --rm -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 myimage:pr-1234 ./run_warmup.sh
```
Ryan: good. If host driver < container expected, you'll see invalid device function or cudaErrorUnknown. Also possible: binary compiled for sm_90 but device reports sm_89.
Sam: nvidia-smi on h100-114 shows Driver Version: 535.86. Container image libcuda reports 535.63. Slight mismatch.
Arjun: that could be enough. Can we try HOST driver 535.113? Or rebuild container against 535.86. Which CUDA toolchain used in the image?
Zoe Lin: image built from upstream cuda:12.2-runtime with nvcc target sm_90. PR 1234 changed some fused kernels recently.
Ryan: FYI setting env CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY sometimes avoids early probe errors but not guaranteed.
Sam: I can try to update host driver to 535.113 (if infra permits) or we can retag the image to use older libcuda. Requesting infra approval.
Sam: @ci-bot rerun job 3456 with tag h100-114-host-check
ci-bot: Rerun queued by Sam for job 3456 on pool h100-nightly. Estimated start in ~2m.
Zoe Lin: monitoring the rerun :eyes:
ci-bot: Rerun started. logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/3456/retry
Sam: rerun failed again. Collected dmesg and nvidia-smi, attaching excerpts.
```
[dmesg excerpt]
NVRM: Xid (0x23) 139, GPU 00000000:00:1e.0: PID 2345: page fault at 0x7f8b...
NVRM: RmInit: GPU 0: NVIDIA H100
```
```
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 12.2      |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Arjun: Xid 139 often indicates a page-fault/PCIe or hardware issue; combined with driver mismatch it's tricky to root remotely. Tagging infra: @infra-team — can you check h100-114 for thermal errors and PCIe resets?
Maria: filing infra ticket 2026-447 with logs and dmesg. I'll attach the CI links.
Ryan: short-term mitigation: mark h100-114 as quarantined or add a filter to not run warmup on that node until infra confirms. Also consider making the warmup test more tolerant (1 retry) so PRs don't get noise.
Zoe Lin: created PR draft to add 2 retries for warmup test and to skip h100-114 via topology label until infra updates node: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-config/pull/789
Sam: infra responded: they saw thermal throttling spikes on h100-114 last night and scheduled a maintenance window. They will attempt driver rollback/firmware patch.
Ryan: thanks. If infra will change host driver, we should schedule a controlled rerun afterward and then run a bisect on PRs that changed kernels (PR 1234 suspect).
Arjun: agree. I'll prepare a bisect script to run the failing kernel unit on h100 after maintenance. Also recommend collecting GPU microcode versions.
Zoe Lin: ci-bot: please keep job 3456 retry limit at 0 for now to avoid masking infra flakiness.
ci-bot: Acknowledged. retry_limit set to 0 for job 3456.
Sam: for the record, manual local run of the image on a different h100 node (h100-101) succeeded once then failed on second run — weird. Could be thermal or PCI instability.
Maria: leaving infra ticket open and will update when maintenance completes.
Zoe Lin: thanks all — leaving bisect/ticket for tomorrow. Will post updates here. :pray:
